title: Continuing Anticoagulants and Antiplatelets in Cold snare Polypectomy.
official: Withdraw or maintain antiplatelets and anticoagulants prior to performing cold snare polypectomy of subcentimeter non-pedunculated colorectal polyps: haemorrhagic and thrombotic risks.
summary: Main objective: To demonstrate that the risk of postpolypectomy hemorrhage (immediate relevant or delayed) of non-pedunculated polyps smaller than 10mm removed with a cold snare, in patients under antiplatelet or anticoagulant treatment, is not higher than that of the control group from which said treatment will have been withdrawn according to the guidelines of current clinical practice
conditions: patients who are requested a colonoscopy for any indication and are under antiplatelet treatment (except ASA) or anticoagulant treatment
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Subjects between 18 and 80 years old for whom a colonoscopy has been requested for any indication
2. Subjects who are under chronic antiplatelet therapy (other than ASA) or anticoagulant treatment.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Coronary stent implantation in the previous 6 months or double antiplatelet therapy.
2. Severe comorbility (ASA >3)
3. Decompensated liver cirrhosis
4. Express refusal to participate in the study.
5. Cardiovascular or thromboembolic event (ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular event, venous thromboembolic disease) in the previous 6 months.
6. Combined treatment with anticoagulants and antiplatelets
7. Chronic kidney disease grade 4 or higher, defined as a Creatinine clearance less than 30 ml/min.
8. Pregnancy or breastfeeding
9. Hemodialysis
10. Thrombophilia or known clotting disorders. Thrombopenia < 50000 platelets/mm3.
11. Urgent colonoscopy
